methods.name: random selection of nonlenses
methods.description: Selecting nonlens samples randomly from the full dataset, excluding those with a lensing galaxy near the central galaxy and those flagged as lenses in other data sets but hard to distinguish visually in DR9 imaging.

methods.name: linear model
methods.description: Initial linear model used to predict labels for training and validation nonlenses to identify and visually remove contamination.

methods.name: cosine similarity calculation
methods.description: Calculating cosine similarity using Faiss without compression techniques on CPU and GPU.

methods.name: linear classification
methods.description: perform linear classification directly on the self-supervised representations

methods.name: oversampling
methods.description: oversampled lenses during fine-tuning to ensure a nonzero average number of lenses in each batch

methods.name: data augmentation
methods.description: augmented images at each training epoch with jitter/crop, random rotations, Gaussian noise, and Gaussian blur

methods.name: minibatch gradient descent
methods.description: Optimization method utilized due to memory constraints introduced by large CNN models and image dimensionality.

methods.name: linear classifier
methods.description: Classifier trained with a single large batch that can handle a high degree of class imbalance.

methods.name: Fine-tuned Self-supervised Classification
methods.description: Attaching a fully connected layer to the 2048-dimensional output of the self-supervised encoder CNN and fine-tuning the network in a supervised setup using lens labels, applying a smaller learning rate to update the CNN encoder parameters and a larger learning rate on the linear classification head initialized randomly.

methods.name: ResNet50
methods.description: Standard encoder network architecture whose convolutional kernels and pooling layers produce a 2048-dimensional representation vector.

methods.name: self-supervised pretraining
methods.description: Pretraining approach that generates differing views of each image using a succession of image augmentations reflecting symmetries, uncertainties, or noise.
